column1: # Numeric conventions (e.g. the 95% multiplier is 2, never 1.96) are hardcoded
# in check_terms.sh itself -- they must also apply inside code chunks and math,
# which the rules below never see.
# House terminology for the book's chapter prose. Read by tools/check_terms.sh,
# which is wired into a PostToolUse hook (.claude/settings.json) so drift gets
# caught in the same edit that introduces it.
# Format: TAB-separated. pattern <TAB> replacement <TAB> skip-line-if <TAB> note
#   pattern        Perl regex. $1..$9 in the replacement refer to its captures.
#   replacement    Literal text plus $N backreferences.
#   skip-line-if   Perl regex; if the raw line matches, this rule is skipped
#                  there. Usually left empty -- the structural exclusions below
#                  already cover most false positives.
#   note           Why. Shown in the checker's output.
# Leave skip-line-if empty by writing two tabs in a row. No non-empty field may
# begin or end with a space, since an editor that trims trailing whitespace
# would silently break the rule. Where a space is load-bearing, assert it with a
# lookaround instead of consuming it -- see the dash rule.
# The checker never looks at fenced chunk bodies (except `#|` option lines,
# which are prose), inline `code` spans, $math$, or HTML comments. That is what
# keeps `zipcode` the column name, geom_boxplot, and the \text{small business}
# table labels out of scope, so most rules need no skip-line-if of their own.
# Adding a rule: put it here, run `./tools/check_terms.sh --all` to see the
# damage, then `--fix`. Do not add a convention a regex can't decide -- those
# belong in the book-style skill, alongside the dollar-sign and probability-scale
# rules.
# Actively drifting terms (round-3 gate, 2026-07-18).
\b[Zz]ip ?code(s?)\b
column4: ZIP code, never zipcode or zip code

column1: \bboxplot(s?)\b
\bZ-score(s?)\b
column4: lowercase z-score; a heading may capitalize it sentence-initially

column1: \b([Ss])mall business (loan|rate)
column4: hyphenate as a compound modifier; standalone "small business" is fine
